business_scope.primary_industry_name: High-End Loose-Leaf Tea Service and Cultural Ceramic Salons

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (Kingdom of Spain, Reino de España)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) – freedom of establishment and capital movement
Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961, in force in Spain since 30 September 1978

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended (including by Real Decreto-ley 7/2021, de 27 de abril, which created the central UBO register); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, approving the implementing Regulation; Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010), Chapter VII on the register book of beneficial owners.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of shareholders' and directors' passports or national identity documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of the country of origin (police/passport office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / company registry extract if a shareholder is a legal entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter from each non-resident shareholder confirming KYC and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating financial institution of the shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax residence certificate / tax identification number of each foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National tax authority of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police background certificate (certificado de antecedentes penales) for all directors and legal representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National criminal records registry of the source country

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of shareholders, directors and UBOs against the Spanish Council of Ministers' PEP list (Orden HAP/211/2018), the consolidated European Union financial sanctions list (EU Council Implementing Regulation), the UN Security Council consolidated list, the OFAC SDN list, and additional domestic risk matrices as per EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 and its amending directives.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) – Sede Electrónica: https://www.rmc.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be original and not confusingly identical to any existing name in the Spanish or EU commercial registry. It may be in any European language but, if not in Spanish, must be transliterated into Latin script. Spanish-language names must follow the orthographic and punctuation rules of the Real Academia Española. The name must not be misleading, unlawful, or contrary to public policy.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In case of rejection, the applicant may file a recurso de alzada before the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado within one month from notification. Alternatively, a new name certificate may be requested with amended alternative names. The granted name is automatically released if the notarial deed is not executed within 90 days; a single 90-day extension may be requested by written application before expiration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as sole registered office because the company must have a physical operational presence in Spain and a specialty tea salon/lounge requires public opening authorisation and municipal licences. Virtual-office services may be used only for auxiliary administrative purposes while a physical operational address is registered.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: projected 70–85% risk during the first financial year due to mandatory health, food-safety and consumer-protection inspections, plus tax-authority monitoring of cash-handling businesses.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Negative name certificate (Certificación Negativa de Denominación) – application for up to 12 proposed names
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee of €16.00 per application, regulated by Spanish official tariffs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) including draft bylaws and signing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary in the registered-office notarial district
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official notarial tariff; typical range €250–€450 for an SL with €3,000 capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Documented Legal Acts tax (Impuesto sobre Actos Jurídicos Documentados) – notarial quota
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Variable regional rate; many communities apply 0% for initial incorporation, otherwise up to 1.5% of the deed's value

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Registry registration filing (inscripción en el Registro Mercantil)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil de la sede social)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registry tariff published in BOE, calculated on share capital and assets; typical for €3,000 SL: €180–€220

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille, notarisation and consular legalisation of foreign documents (per dossier, up to 10 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority in the foreign jurisdiction (Ministry of Foreign Affairs or designated notary) and optionally Spanish Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fees fixed by issuing authority; typical notarial and apostille costs €80–€150

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NIE (Foreigner Identification Number) application processing for each non-resident shareholder/director
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Consular Office or Spanish National Police (Comisaría General de Extranjería)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative tax and consular fee of €9–€20 per person plus service charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation AML/UBO due diligence report (UBO piercing, PEP/sanctions screening, source of funds verification)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External law firm (market benchmark, fixed fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for legal due diligence in Madrid/Barcelona; typical range €500–€900

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provisional municipal activity licence application and pre-assessment for the tea lounge premises
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Municipal Ayuntamiento – Urbanism and Activities Department
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Local tax and administrative fee; commonly €200–€400 for food-and-beverage small business, per municipal ordinance

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), including Articles 4, 20-24, 58-62, 78-82, 210-245, 247-252, 279-284, and 319-345; Royal Decree 1784/1996 approving the Mercantile Registry Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the company's registered office; company-name clearance is obtained from the Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), together with the certified company-name clearance, filed for registration with the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The minimum share capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. Until equity reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve and, on liquidation with insufficient assets, shareholders may have joint and several liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and the company's net assets. A statutory escrow account is not required, although a bank certificate of contribution may be used; an incorporation declaration may replace the certificate under applicable law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the Company accepts the subscription and full payment of its share capital by the founding shareholder in accordance with the incorporation deed; (2) the registered office is adopted at the address stated in the deed and articles; (3) the Company's corporate purpose is conducted only after obtaining all required municipal, food-service, safety, and other permits; (4) [Name] is appointed sole director, or the directors named in the deed are confirmed, with authority to represent the Company; and (5) the officers are authorized to execute filings, open bank accounts, obtain tax registrations, and complete all incorporation formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), certification portal or authorized filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed name and alternatives, identifying the intended legal form as Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. Obtain the original negative name certificate and reserve the name for the statutory validity period. Foreign founders should ensure that names and powers are consistent with their identity documents.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
Foreign document legalization or apostille, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected, submit an alternative name or cure the stated similarity, prohibited-term, or documentation defect and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Selected Spanish notary public and, for non-resident shareholders, the competent consular or apostille authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of association, corporate purpose, registered office, share capital, share allocation, governance model, director details, and beneficial-ownership information. Obtain a bank contribution certificate where cash capital is deposited, or include the legally permitted founder declaration. Legalize, apostille, and translate foreign corporate documents and powers as required.
required_dossiers: Founder passports or national identity documents
Spanish foreigner identification numbers (NIE), where required
Bank certificate of capital contribution or permitted founder declaration
Foreign shareholder corporate extracts and board approvals
Notarized and apostilled powers of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistent names, powers, capital data, articles, translations, or beneficial-owner information before execution of the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public (Notaría) selected by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary personally or through a valid power of attorney. Execute the escritura pública de constitución, articles, capital statement, director acceptance, and beneficial-owner identification. Request certified copies and the electronic notarial filing where available.
required_dossiers: Capital contribution evidence or permitted declaration
Legalized foreign powers and corporate authorizations
Translations by an authorized sworn translator, where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure notarial observations by supplying missing evidence, correcting the deed, or executing a supplemental or rectifying public instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Provisional Tax Identification and File Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) and the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 036 with the AEAT for the provisional NIF and tax census registration. Submit the public deed, articles, provisional NIF, name certificate, and required forms to the Provincial Mercantile Registry within the statutory filing period. Pay applicable notarial, registry, publication, and agent charges; these are not state incorporation filing fees.
required_dossiers: Registry filing forms and fee payment evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a registry qualification notice within the applicable correction period, amend or supplement the deed, and resubmit through the notary or filing agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry and Spanish State Tax Administration Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the registered deed and obtain the definitive NIF by filing the registered deed and final Form 036 information with the AEAT. Register the appropriate economic activity headings, tax obligations, director status, and accounting obligations. Obtain an electronic certificate for the company and record the ownership and governance information in the corporate books.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax census inconsistencies, provide missing registry evidence, or submit an amended Form 036 and supporting documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Municipal Premises and Operating Authorizations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal council (Ayuntamiento) licensing, urban-planning, and environmental department at the premises location; applicable autonomous-community food and labor authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before opening, determine whether the premises require a prior activity/opening licence or may use a responsible declaration (declaración responsable) under local law. Submit the technical project, premises plans, accessibility and fire documentation, acoustic study where required, waste arrangements, food-service information, and proof of tax registration. Do not commence operations until the applicable filing or permit becomes effective.
required_dossiers: Acoustic and environmental documentation, where required
Responsible declaration or prior licence application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer municipal technical observations, amend the project, pay supplementary fees, request an inspection, or appeal an express refusal under the applicable administrative procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The competent Ayuntamiento municipal licensing department, coordinated where applicable with the relevant autonomous-community industrial, health, environmental, and labor authorities. Spain has no single national hospitality operating-licence board.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal activity and opening licence (licencia de actividad y apertura) or, where permitted by the municipality, responsible declaration for commencement of activity (declaración responsable de inicio de actividad) for a tea lounge, hospitality premises, and food-service operation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico), or the designated environmental authority of the relevant autonomous community
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Normally exempt from a formal project-level EIA for an ordinary existing-premises specialty tea lounge without significant industrial installations; municipal environmental, acoustic, waste, and activity controls still apply. A formal assessment may arise from major construction, protected-location impacts, significant emissions, or autonomous-community rules.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with municipal and autonomous-community wastewater discharge limits, sewer pre-treatment requirements, grease and solid-waste controls where applicable, and licensed waste transfer rules. Avoid uncontrolled VOC, odor, smoke, and combustion emissions; commercial kitchens must meet applicable ventilation and extraction requirements. Hazardous waste, if any, must be segregated and transferred through authorized waste managers. Exact numerical limits depend on the municipality, sewer authority, equipment, and autonomous-community legislation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain the municipal fire-safety and occupancy compliance documentation required for the premises, including evacuation routes, emergency lighting, extinguishers, fire-resistant installations, and maximum occupancy. Provide structural-load certification where alterations, heavy equipment, or increased occupancy require it. Complete electrical, gas, ventilation, accessibility, and health-and-safety inspections; establish occupational risk prevention, worker training, food hygiene controls, and emergency procedures before opening.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT. The AEAT administers the Spanish tax identification number (NIF), VAT registration, census registration, VAT returns, customs tax procedures, and intra-Community VAT identification. Customs matters are administered through the AEAT Department of Customs and Excise Duties.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must obtain a provisional NIF during incorporation and convert it into a definitive NIF after registration of the deed and articles with the Commercial Registry. The application is generally filed with AEAT Form 036, electronically through the AEAT portal by an authorized person or tax representative. The filing package normally includes the notarized incorporation deed, articles of association, Commercial Registry evidence, identification of directors and authorized representatives, registered office details, activity codes, expected commencement date, VAT obligations, and beneficial-owner information where requested. Foreign shareholders and directors generally require a Spanish NIF or NIE, or an assigned foreign-entity NIF where applicable. A non-resident shareholder or foreign entity requesting a Spanish NIF must provide identity and existence documents, evidence of authority, and a Spanish tax representative or power of attorney where required; foreign public documents normally require apostille or legalization and an official Spanish translation. The company must also register its economic activities and tax census information through Form 036. Registration in the Register of Intra-Community Operators (ROI) and activation of the VIES VAT number require a separate Form 036 request and may be subject to AEAT verification of the intended intra-Community activity. Importers and exporters generally require an EORI number obtained through AEAT customs procedures.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Spanish SL is generally subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal person; there is no general United States-style check-the-box election to treat an SL as a fiscally transparent entity. The entity may elect or qualify for specific statutory regimes, including the consolidated tax group regime, the special regime for entities qualifying as newly created companies, the regime for small entities where applicable, the special regime for holding companies of foreign participations (ETVE) where conditions are met, and other sector-specific or restructuring regimes. These regimes do not generally convert an ordinary SL into a partnership-style pass-through entity. Spanish anti-hybrid mismatch rules may deny deductions, impose inclusion, or otherwise neutralize mismatches involving foreign transparent or opaque classifications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA), the Spanish Value Added Tax system, supplemented by customs VAT on imports and special territorial rules for the Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla. Mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands are within the EU VAT territory; the Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla are outside EU VAT territory and have separate indirect-tax regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general Spanish VAT registration threshold applies to a business established in Spain. A Spanish SL carrying out taxable economic activities must register in the tax census before commencing the activity and charge VAT where its supplies are taxable in Spain. The EUR 85,000 annual threshold under the EU small-business scheme is not a general exemption threshold currently available for treating an ordinary Spanish-established business as outside Spanish VAT; eligibility depends on the applicable EU small-enterprise regime and implementing rules. Separate thresholds and obligations may apply to distance sales, intra-Community acquisitions, special regimes, and specific territorial supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time invoice-clearance requirement for all businesses. Taxpayers subject to the Immediate Supply of Information regime (Suministro Inmediato de Información, SII), including qualifying large businesses, VAT groups, REDEME entities, and voluntary participants, must transmit specified invoice-record data electronically to AEAT generally within four calendar days, subject to statutory exceptions and an eight-day rule for invoices issued by the recipient or a third party. The VERI*FACTU and certified billing-system framework under Royal Decree 1007/2023 requires covered billing software to preserve integrity, traceability, accessibility, and anti-tampering records; applicable implementation dates and technical specifications must be confirmed against current transitional legislation and AEAT guidance. The general B2B electronic-invoicing obligation under Law 18/2022 is being phased in after its implementing regulation and statutory timing conditions; it should not be treated as an immediate universal clearance mandate. Electronic invoices must satisfy Spanish VAT invoicing requirements, including issuer and customer identification, sequential numbering, date, taxable base, VAT rate, VAT amount, and legally required special-regime references.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.locality_specific_notes: A specialty tea salon located in mainland Spain or the Balearic Islands generally applies 21% VAT to prepared beverages, restaurant or hospitality services, and most ancillary taxable supplies, subject to the specific classification of the supply. Certain food products may qualify for reduced rates, but the rate must be determined by the nature and presentation of each product. The Canary Islands use IGIC rather than mainland Spanish VAT, while Ceuta and Melilla use separate local indirect-tax treatment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched from mainland Spain or the Balearic Islands to destinations outside the EU VAT territory may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT, provided the goods leave the EU customs territory and the exporter can substantiate the export. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for VAT exemption where the customer is VAT-identified in another EU Member State, the goods are transported from Spain to that Member State, and the supplier satisfies invoicing, transport evidence, and recapitulative-statement requirements. Services are not automatically treated as exported goods. A B2B service supplied to a business established outside Spain may be outside Spanish VAT under the general place-of-supply rule, subject to exceptions for services connected with immovable property, admission to events, passenger transport, short-term hiring of transport, restaurant and catering, and other special categories. Input VAT refunds require valid invoices, actual business use, deductibility, and compliance with the applicable VAT return or non-established-business refund procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration accepted by Spanish Customs, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN) and export-release or exit confirmation
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, customer, goods, value, delivery terms, and destination
Packing list and transport document, such as a bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or equivalent
Proof of physical exit from the EU customs territory, such as customs exit results, carrier confirmation, or equivalent electronic evidence
For intra-Community supplies: customer VAT identification number validated through VIES, transport evidence, and the required EC Sales List or equivalent recapitulative statement
Evidence linking the exported goods to the relevant sales invoice, customs declaration, accounting records, and payment records where requested

Inward-remittance evidence is not a universal Spanish VAT export requirement, but bank records and payment evidence should be retained where relevant to demonstrate the underlying transaction and respond to an AEAT audit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated within 180 days. AEAT may deny or reverse the VAT exemption where the goods did not leave the EU, the export evidence is incomplete or inconsistent, the customer VAT number is invalid, transport is not substantiated, or the transaction is fictitious. The resulting VAT may be assessed retrospectively, together with late-payment interest and applicable penalties. Incorrect VAT treatment may attract penalties commonly calculated by reference to the unpaid or improperly deducted tax, with higher exposure for concealment, fraudulent conduct, repeated non-compliance, false invoices, or bookkeeping manipulation. Undue input-VAT refunds may be clawed back with interest and penalties. Customs infringements may additionally result in customs debt, import or export restrictions, seizure, and administrative penalties. Intentional fraud may create criminal tax exposure where statutory tax-loss thresholds and other criminal-law requirements are met. Records supporting exports, invoices, transport, customs clearance, and VAT returns should generally be retained for the applicable Spanish statutory limitation and record-preservation periods, commonly at least four years for tax assessment purposes, with longer retention potentially required for accounting, customs, or capital-goods adjustment purposes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain maintains full capital account convertibility as an EU member state. Current account transactions including profit remittances face no prior approval requirements. Corporate dividends may be repatriated freely to shareholders at market rates subject only to standard tax reporting and beneficial ownership verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion ratios apply to export proceeds. Service receipts from specialty tea salon operations are classified as current account items and converted at prevailing market rates without statutory timelines.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for Bank of Spain-regulated e-money institutions under EU MiCA framework. Legal constraints include mandatory AML/KYC compliance and restrictions on unlicensed offshore digital wallet activities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding permitted via video KYC and electronic document verification for Spanish SL entities. Physical director presence not required for standard accounts but may be mandated for high-value transactions or enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening or adverse media hits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source of funds statements, beneficial ownership certificates, and legal entity verification documents

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or PEP exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized ownership structure, shareholder agreements, tax residency proofs, and enhanced due diligence reports

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing via SEPA transfers to Spanish IBAN accounts using purpose codes such as 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION' or 'SHARE CAPITAL INJECTION'. Verification requires matching remitter details with KYC profiles and board resolutions for non-standard amounts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails include SWIFT MT103 for international wires and Commercial Letters of Credit for supplier settlements. Local or EU supplier payments processed via SEPA with remittance advice.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency swaps and cross-currency basis swaps

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) and filing with the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Central / Provincial Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of approval by the shareholders' meeting; accounts must be approved within 6 months of the fiscal year-end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties scaled to turnover: minimum EUR 1,200 (approx. USD 1,300) for small companies, up to EUR 60,000 (approx. USD 65,000) for repeated non-filing; closure of the company's tax registration; risk of administrative strike-off after prolonged default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Form 200/220)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the end of the 6-month period after the tax year-end; due 1–25 July for entities with a 31 December fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharges: 5% on tax amount (up to 20% after 12 months) plus late-payment interest; penalty up to 150% of the tax due for inaccurate or fraudulent returns

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT Return (Modelo 390, annual summary) and VAT settlement (Modelo 303)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Modelo 303 due within the first 20 calendar days of each quarter; Modelo 390 annual summary due 1–30 January following the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharges 5%–20% of amount due plus interest; penalty up to USD 6,500 for non-substantiated or late returns

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBO) confirmation and update filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil / Official UBO Registry (register of ultimate beneficial owners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation alongside the annual accounts filing; any changes in UBO must be filed within 1 month of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EUR 10,000 (approx. USD 10,800) for inaccurate UBO data; repeated non-compliance may lead to administrative strike-off and prohibition on registration operations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Activities Tax declaration (IAE) for local business operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) / Local Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing for changes in activity or turnover variables by 1 March; registration is required before commencement of business
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Municipal penalties for failure to register or update activity, ranging from EUR 600 to EUR 3,000 (approx. USD 650 to USD 3,250)

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required for two consecutive years if the company meets at least two of the following: total assets exceed EUR 2.85 million (approx. USD 3.1 million); annual net turnover exceeds EUR 5.7 million (approx. USD 6.2 million); average number of employees exceeds 50. Exempt for most small SL tea salons but mandatory if parent-subsidiary links or specific sectors apply
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad, PGC), which is converged with IFRS for consolidated companies; small- and medium-sized entities use PGC PYMES

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must maintain a statutory register of ultimate beneficial owners and file annual updates with the Mercantile Registry. Any transfer of shares or changes in controlling ownership must be formally recorded in the member register and the UBO register and notified to the Registry within one month of the relevant notarial deed or board resolution
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
